intent: enterprise tests: fix conftest sys.path + silence starlette httpx deprecation
notes: Fix Finding #8 from Session 3 (four enterprise test files failing at collection). `enterprise/tests/conftest.py` didn't put `enterprise/` on `sys.path`, so `pytest enterprise/tests/` from the repo root failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app'` for `test_api_contract.py`, `test_error_envelope.py`, `test_rate_limit.py`, `test_views.py`. All 4 files import from `app.*`. Added a `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` for both `enterprise/` (makes `app` importable) and `enterprise/enterprise-cli/` (makes `gator_enterprise_cli` importable — the pattern the individual test files were doing themselves as workarounds can be dropped in a future cleanup, but leaving them for now to avoid touching working files unnecessarily). After the fix: 49 previously-uncollectable tests all pass on first run — pure config gap, no runtime issues.

Fix Finding #7 from Session 3 (StarletteDeprecationWarning cluttering test output). Starlette 1.4.1 prefers `httpx2` over `httpx` for its testclient and warns on fallback. The recommendation ("install `httpx2`") is real but adds two runtime deps (httpx2 + httpcore2) without any functional benefit — testclient works fine with httpx. Chose to filter the warning instead. Requires both `warnings.filterwarnings()` (for import-time warnings that fire before pytest's warning-capture takes over) AND `pytest_configure` registering a `filterwarnings` inivalue (because pytest re-enables warnings via its `catch_warnings` context and would otherwise surface the filtered warning in the summary regardless of the Python-level filter). Neither hook alone suffices — the doc-comment explains why. When the underlying dep migrates or the warning changes, this filter becomes a no-op or gets updated.
End-to-end verified: all enterprise tests now run and pass — 133 passed, 1 skipped, no warnings summary. Full detail in `.gator/vault/artifacts/2026-08-06-enterprise-local-bringup-session-log.md`.
Doesn't touch product code or charters. Test infrastructure only.
